newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM QUARTELY OUTPUT RISES, SALES SLUMP.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM QUARTELY OUTPUT RISES, SALES SLUMP.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) copper production in the quarter ended September 30 exceeded that of the corresponding 1995 quarter but copper sales slumped due to operational problems, a group spokesman said.
The spokesman said copper output, at 80,372 tonnes was 6,747 tonnes higher than the 73,625 realised in the 1995 quarter.

However, copper sales from the company's own production, at 73,575 tonnes were lower than the 79,414 tonnes realised in the 1995 quater due to operational problems at the Tanzania Zambia railway (TAZRA) linking it to the port of Dar-es-Salaam.
"In spite of higher production, sales were adversely affected by operational problems on the Tanzania-Zambia railway line," the spokesman said.
"Sales, including metal bought-in, were 94,292 tonnes for the quarter, compared to 133,305 tonnes in the corresponding period of the previous year," the spokesman added.
Cobalt production, at 1,155 tonnes for the quarter, was 73 percent higher than the 667 tonnes in the previous year's quarter, due to the availability of high grade Nchanga copper concentrate.
Cobalt sales, at 1,146 tonnes, were 125 percent higher than the 509 tonnes sold in the 1995 quarter.
Total sales revenue for the quarter decreased by 27 percent to 290,125 million kwacha.

"In spite of the depreciation of the kwacha between the corresponding period of the previous year and the period under review, lower copper prices, and lower cobalt prices, together with reduced copper sales volumes, contributed to the reduction in sales revenue," the spokesman said.
"However, the high volume of cobalt sales made a positive contribution during the quarter under review," he added.
The average sales realisation in the quarter, at 2.035 million kwacha per tonne, was 23 percent lower that that of the corresponding quarter.
The average sales realisation for cobalt was 49.9 million kwacha per tonne from 52.803 kwacha in the previous quarter.
Revenue from sales of precious metals amounted to 1,491 million kwacha during the quarter, compared to 448 million during the 1995 quarter.
The group recorded an operating loss of 55,539 million for the quarter, against a profit of 40,744 million in the 1995 quarter.

"After taking into consideration exchange losses, interest, taxation charges and other items, the group made a net loss of 95,837 million, compared to a net loss of 7,374 million in the same period of 1995," the spokesman said.
The board of directors had not declared a dividend in respect of the quarter ended September 30, he added.
